items.headline: Two more tankers hit by projectiles near Hormuz as US calls its blockade of Iran 'ironclad'
items.summary: Two oil tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles near the strait; five Indian crew were rescued from one. The US defense secretary said the blockade of Iranian ports is ironclad.
items.rationale: Continued strikes keep war-risk insurance and freight rates high and sustain a crude risk premium, hurting Asian importers most.

industries.why: Tanker insurance and crew risk rise

economies.why: Crude importer with crews at risk

items.headline: Iran's rial hits record low near 2.7 million per dollar as blockade halts oil loadings
items.summary: Iran loaded no oil in September, a first since 1979, and oil already at sea may run out by mid-October. The rial fell to about 2.7 million per dollar; inflation is near 90%.
items.rationale: Iran's export collapse removes barrels from the market and raises the risk of desperate escalation against Gulf shipping.

economies.why: Loses main source of discounted crude

items.headline: Hormuz LNG transits reach 19 cargoes in September, highest since the war began
items.summary: Nineteen LNG cargoes left the strait in September, 13 from Qatar and six from the UAE, up from 15 in June. If the pace holds, October transits could recover to about 25% of pre-war levels.
items.rationale: Partial LNG recovery eases gas shortages in Asia and Europe, but volumes remain far below normal, keeping prices elevated.

industries.why: More cargoes cap gas price upside

items.headline: Saudi Arabia plans offensive to retake Bab el-Mandeb from the Houthis, with up to 100,000 troops
items.summary: Riyadh is preparing an assault, led by Yemeni ground forces with Saudi air support, to reverse Houthi control of Bab el-Mandeb. Over 100,000 troops could be mobilised in the coming weeks.
items.rationale: Fighting at a second chokepoint raises near-term Red Sea shipping risk, though success could reopen the route and lower freight costs later.

industries.why: Red Sea route risk rises before any reopening

items.headline: Brent ends the week near $102.70, up about 7% over the past month
items.summary: Brent traded at $102.70 on October 3. Over the month to October 3 it ranged from $93.15 to $109.97, averaging $101.08, a 6.92% gain.
items.rationale: Crude above $100 keeps fuel, freight and headline inflation high, squeezing importers and pushing central banks to stay tight.

economies.why: Higher prices for exporters still shipping

items.headline: OPEC+ meets October 4, with targets expected to be rolled over at September levels
items.summary: OPEC+ countries making monthly adjustments meet October 4, with physical supply still below February levels. A rollover at September 2026 levels is expected; core members held policy unchanged on 6 September.
items.rationale: No extra supply from producers leaves the market reliant on Hormuz recovery, keeping prices supported.

items.headline: S&P 500 ends week at 7,722.72, slightly down, as payrolls rise only 29,000
items.summary: The Dow fell 651.66 points on the week to 51,176.96 and the S&P 500 slipped 20.69, while the Nasdaq rose 122.15 to 27,190.86. September payrolls grew 29,000; unemployment rose to 4.2%.
items.rationale: A stalling labour market cuts near-term hike risk and helps growth stocks, but signals slower consumer demand and earnings.

industries.why: Nasdaq gains as rate fears ease
Weak hiring points to softer spending

items.headline: Odds of an October Fed hike fall to about 17% after weak jobs data
items.summary: CME FedWatch showed about a 17% chance of an October quarter-point hike, and prediction markets 18%, down from almost 70% a week earlier. A December hike is still priced; the Fed meets October 27–28.
items.rationale: A likely pause eases pressure on yields and the dollar, helping rate-sensitive sectors and emerging-market currencies.

items.headline: Yen weakens to about 158.4 per dollar as markets halve bets on an October BoJ hike
items.summary: After the BoJ's Summary of Opinions, pricing for an October hike roughly halved and USD/JPY rose 0.5% to 158.44. Analysts now expect the next hike in December; the policy rate is 1.25%.
items.rationale: A softer yen lifts exporters' profits but raises the cost of imported fuel and food, and keeps intervention risk alive.

items.headline: India's forex reserves post record $18.3 billion weekly drop as the RBI defends the rupee
items.summary: Reserves fell $18.3 billion in a week, the largest on record, and $38.1 billion over three weeks from a $785.7 billion peak. The RBI meets October 5–7, with a hike to 5.5% expected.
items.rationale: Heavy intervention and a likely rate hike signal acute currency stress from oil prices, tightening domestic credit conditions.

items.headline: Ukraine weighs four proposals for a Black Sea and energy truce, calling India's the most comprehensive
items.summary: Kyiv received truce proposals from the US, India, Turkey and Egypt. India's plan would halt attacks on all energy facilities, including ports. Ukraine wants energy and Black Sea ceasefires linked.
items.rationale: A truce would ease grain and fuel shipping risk in the Black Sea, lowering wheat and freight premiums; talks are early.

industries.why: Black Sea shipping risk may fall

items.headline: Euro-area inflation jumps to 3.8% in September on 18.8% energy price rise
items.summary: Eurostat's flash estimate showed inflation at 3.8% from 3.2%, above the 3.6% forecast, the highest since 2023. Core inflation edged up to 2.5%. The ECB hiked on 10 September.
items.rationale: Energy-led inflation raises the odds of another ECB hike, lifting borrowing costs while squeezing household incomes.
